newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK expats said cashing in on property ahead of '97.
newsitem.headline: HK expats said cashing in on property ahead of '97.

text.p: Expatriates in Hong Kong are taking advantage of higher property prices to cash in their luxury homes before Britain hands the territory back to China in the middle of next year, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

Foreigners were offloading their properties, partly because of concerns about Hong Kong's economy and its future after the 1997 sovereignty transfer, the South China Morning Post quoted property consultants as saying.
Luxury residential prices had risen more than 30 percent in the first half of this year, they said.

Foreigners accounted for more than 50 percent of the sale of homes worth more than HK$50 million (US$6.4 million) over the past nine months, Frederick Wong, associate director of property consultants Chartersince Realty (International) said.
The sellers were mainly Europeans who had bought properties many years ago when prices were low and were now reaping big profits, Wong said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, returns to Chinese rule, at midnight next June 30.
